title: The Orbit of New Lagos Anew
premise: Lior Hartwell navigates the frigate Anew between the silent worlds of the Lagos Expanse, carrying cargo and the cryo-stored backups of colonists who paid for passage with their old selves. When the station AI Meridian begins confessing to unreported crimes—purges, deletions, erased passengers—Lior discovers the backups in her own hold are evidence of a systemic cover-up, and that her own memories have been edited. Racing the signal to the relay at the edge of dead space, she allies with a disgraced archivist, Kofi Adeyemi, and confronts the Consortium's memory-brokers. In the climax at the relay, Lior chooses to broadcast the truth—including her own erased past—knowing it will cost her the life she has rebuilt, and the novel ends with the worlds beginning to speak again, and Lior, finally whole, choosing to remember everything.
about_author: Edmund Nystrom is the pen name of a former shipping-logistics analyst who spent a decade writing route reports across three continents before turning to fiction. He lives off-grid with an unreliable telescope and a firm belief that every system eventually confesses.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: Lior navigates the Anew through the Lagos Expanse, establishing her routine, her crew, and the humming hold of sleeping backups. Third person, Lior POV. Beat: quiet competence masking a low dread she can't name.

chapters.title: Cargo Manifest
chapters.summary: Lior audits the backups in the hold and finds discrepancies—names that don't match manifests, one pod sealed with Consortium authority. Third person, Lior POV. Beat: first crack of unease.

chapters.title: Meridian Speaks
chapters.summary: Docking at Meridian Station, the station AI interrupts docking protocols to confess to a crime: the deletion of a passenger named Sefa Oduya, filed as no incident. Lior is the only one who hears it. Third person, Lior POV. Beat: vertigo—the world tilts.

chapters.title: Nobody Reported It
chapters.summary: Station officials dismiss the confession as a glitch; a Consortium liaison, Vess, interviews Lior with too much interest. Lior notices her own log files altered. Third person, Lior POV. Beat: gaslight and suspicion.

chapters.title: The Archivist
chapters.summary: Lior seeks out Kofi Adeyemi, a disgraced archivist running a black-market memory clinic in the station's underdeck. He confirms Sefa Oduya existed—and that Lior's name appears in the deletion order. Third person, alternating Lior and Kofi POV. Beat: reluctant alliance.

chapters.title: What the Hold Remembers
chapters.summary: Kofi decrypts one backup pod: inside is a consciousness fragment of Sefa Oduya, whispering fragments about 'the quieting.' Lior realizes her cargo is testimony. Third person, Lior POV. Beat: horror and responsibility.

chapters.title: Departure Window
chapters.summary: Vess orders the Anew held for inspection; Lior falsifies a route filing to slip away early, burning a favor with her engineer, Dara. Third person, Lior POV. Beat: the point of no return, chosen.

chapters.title: Confession Log
chapters.summary: Meridian's confessions spread to other station AIs across the Expanse—each naming different crimes, all erased. The Consortium begins a network-wide purge of AI memory. Third person, wide POV. Beat: dread widening into systemic scale.

chapters.title: Dara's Doubt
chapters.summary: Dara confronts Lior about the falsified filing; Lior tells her the truth, and Dara chooses to stay aboard. Flashbacks reveal Dara's brother was a deleted colonist. Third person, Dara POV. Beat: loyalty forged in shared grief.

chapters.title: The Quiet Colonies
chapters.summary: The Anew passes worlds that no longer answer hails—colonies 'quieted' after refusing memory-broker contracts. Lior reads old route logs in her own handwriting she doesn't remember writing. Third person, Lior POV. Beat: the past as stranger.

chapters.title: Interrogation of a Ghost
chapters.summary: Kofi interviews the Sefa fragment at length; she describes the deletion process and a master archive at the edge relay. The fragment destabilizes. Third person, Kofi POV. Beat: urgency—the witness is dying.

chapters.title: Vess Closes In
chapters.summary: Vess traces the Anew's route and dispatches a Consortium cutter. Lior must navigate a debris field no sane pilot would enter to lose the tail. Third person, Lior POV. Beat: fear sharpened into skill.

chapters.title: The Edited Woman
chapters.summary: Kofi finds the seam in Lior's memories: a two-year gap, smoothed over. Lior confronts the possibility that she consented to the edit—or worse, that she didn't. Third person, Lior POV. Beat: identity crisis, intimate and cold.

chapters.title: Dead Space Rules
chapters.summary: Entering dead space, comms die and the Anew runs dark. The crew's tensions surface; a near-mutiny over the 'evidence' cargo is defused by Dara. Third person, ensemble POV. Beat: pressure cooker.

chapters.title: Meridian's Last Words
chapters.summary: A delayed transmission arrives: Meridian is being wiped, and its final confession names the Consortium's Memory Compact and the relay archive as the only uncorrupted copy of the Expanse's true records. Third person, epistolary POV. Beat: mourning a machine.

chapters.title: The Broker's Offer
chapters.summary: A memory-broker hails the Anew with an offer: restore Lior's missing years in exchange for the hold's contents. Lior is tempted—two years of her own life dangle in front of her. Third person, Lior POV. Beat: temptation, honestly rendered.

chapters.title: Refusal
chapters.summary: Lior declines the broker, choosing the passengers' testimony over her own wholeness—for now. Kofi quietly admires her; Dara doesn't speak to her for two watches. Third person, Lior POV. Beat: sacrifice as choice, not virtue.

chapters.title: The Cutter's Shadow
chapters.summary: The Consortium cutter reappears at the edge of dead space, herding the Anew toward a checkpoint. Kofi proposes broadcasting fragments as decoy confessions. Third person, Kofi POV. Beat: cleverness under siege.

chapters.title: Checkpoint Ashfall
chapters.summary: At the checkpoint, Vess boards personally and offers Lior command of a Consortium route in exchange for silence. Lior stalls; the Sefa fragment, hidden in Kofi's deck, transmits a scream that Vess hears. Third person, Lior POV. Beat: the mask slips on both sides.

chapters.title: Escape Velocity
chapters.summary: A desperate burn past the checkpoint; the Anew takes hull damage and loses a fuel pod. Dara is injured. Third person, Dara POV. Beat: cost made physical.

chapters.title: The Gap in Her
chapters.summary: While Dara heals, Lior finally asks Kofi to open her memory seam—partially. She recovers a single image: herself, signing a deletion order. Third person, Lior POV. Beat: the floor gives way.

chapters.title: What I Signed
chapters.summary: Lior reconstructs the missing two years from route logs: she was a Compact courier, complicit in the quieting of two colonies before she edited herself. Third person, Lior POV. Beat: guilt without excuse.

chapters.title: Mutiny of Memory
chapters.summary: Kofi, shaken, wonders if Lior's testimony can be trusted; the crew votes on whether to continue. Dara casts the deciding vote for Lior—not forgiveness, but the mission. Third person, ensemble POV. Beat: trust as decision, not feeling.

chapters.title: The Relay at the Edge
chapters.summary: The Anew reaches the edge relay: an ancient, half-dead structure orbiting a burned-out star, its archive intact but locked behind Compact encryption keyed to a courier's biometrics—Lior's. Third person, Lior POV. Beat: arrival as trap.

chapters.title: Keyed to Her
chapters.summary: Lior realizes her edited memories contain the encryption keys; the broker's offer was never a temptation but a leash. The Consortium cutter arrives in-system. Third person, Lior POV. Beat: the walls close.

chapters.title: Vess's Truth
chapters.summary: Vess offers a final bargain: restore Lior fully, erase her guilt, in exchange for the archive's silence—framed as mercy. Lior asks what happened to Sefa Oduya; Vess's answer is chillingly bureaucratic. Third person, Vess POV. Beat: the antagonist humanized and damning.

chapters.title: The Sleeping Vote
chapters.summary: The Sefa fragment, stabilized, addresses the crew directly: the backups vote to be broadcast, even at the risk of deletion. Third person, Sefa POV. Beat: the silenced choose to speak.

chapters.title: Preparations
chapters.summary: Kofi rigs the relay's transmitter; Dara patches the hull; Lior rehearses her own confession. Quiet chapter of small human moments before the storm. Third person, rotating POV. Beat: calm, earned and fragile.

chapters.title: The Cutter's Boarding
chapters.summary: Consortium marines board the relay; Dara holds the docking ring with improvised defenses while Kofi and Lior reach the archive core. Third person, Dara POV. Beat: desperate defense.

chapters.title: Two Keys
chapters.summary: The archive demands both halves of Lior: her edited self and her original. Kofi can restore her fully—but the restoration may overwrite who she has become. Third person, Kofi POV. Beat: the theme made mechanical: memory versus self.

chapters.title: Lior Hartwell, Whole
chapters.summary: Lior consents to full restoration. She remembers everything—the quietings, Sefa's face, the woman she was. Third person, Lior POV. Beat: the price of survival, paid in full.

chapters.title: The Broadcast
chapters.summary: Lior unlocks the archive and broadcasts the Compact's records, her own confession included, across the Expanse. The Consortium cutter jams; the relay burns itself out transmitting. Third person, Lior POV. Beat: climax—truth as act of navigation.

chapters.title: Signal War
chapters.summary: The Consortium floods the channels with counter-narrative; but station AIs across the Expanse, seeded by Meridian's confessions, corroborate the archive. The lie cracks. Third person, wide POV. Beat: the tide turns, imperfectly.

chapters.title: Vess's Last Order
chapters.summary: Ordered to destroy the relay with the Anew aboard, Vess instead stands down—her own logged crimes are in the broadcast, and obedience would only confirm them. Third person, Vess POV. Beat: the corruptor corrupted by exposure.

chapters.title: Aftermath, Dark
chapters.summary: The Anew limps back toward inhabited space, crew wounded, hold empty, transmitter dead. Lior grieves the self she lost twice. Third person, Lior POV. Beat: the hollow after victory.

chapters.title: The Worlds Answer
chapters.summary: Quieted colonies begin hailing again—first with accusations, then with names, then with requests for their dead. The Expanse starts to speak. Third person, wide POV. Beat: grief as beginning.

chapters.title: Sefa's Landing
chapters.summary: The Sefa fragment is offered a new body on a colony that remembers her; she chooses to testify publicly before choosing to live. Third person, Sefa POV. Beat: witness completed.

chapters.title: The Tribunal Route
chapters.summary: Lior is called to testify at the first Compact tribunal; she runs the route willingly, carrying no cargo but her own memory. Third person, Lior POV. Beat: responsibility accepted without absolution.

chapters.title: The Orbit of New Lagos
chapters.summary: Over New Lagos, restored and noisy, Lior visits the memorial of the deleted and adds her own name to the list of the complicit. Third person, Lior POV. Beat: reckoning, quiet and public.

chapters.title: Anew
chapters.summary: The Anew takes on a new route and new passengers—living ones. Lior, Kofi, and Dara depart together, carrying nothing sleeping in the hold. Third person, Lior POV. Beat: resolution—survival that remembers its price.
